title: "Usage"
---

## Local Development

Prerequisites:

- Python 3.11, managed through `uv`.
- Quarto on `PATH` for docs and snapshot/site rendering.
- Snowflake credentials only when running `export-snowflake` against real data.

Set up the environment:

```bash
uv sync --dev
```

Run the core checks:

```bash
uv run pytest
quarto render docs
```

## Portable Report Commands

| Command | Purpose | Writes real data? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uv run aots-report snapshot --baseline <dir> --out <dir>` | Validate a baseline, regenerate a Report Snapshot, compare outputs, and render an audit site. | No Snowflake access; reads local baseline artifacts. |
| `uv run aots-report export-snowflake ... --dry-run --json` | Show the read-only Snowflake export plan without connecting or writing files. | No. |
| `uv run aots-report export-snowflake ... --out <dir>` | Export a local Known-Good Baseline from Snowflake source artifacts. | Yes, but only to local ignored output. |
| `uv run aots-report publish --snapshots-dir <dir> --out <dir>` | Build a publication manifest and index over Snapshot Output Bundles. | No. |

## Fixture Meanings

- `tests/fixtures/synthetic_baseline/` is a smoke fixture. It proves CLI wiring, validation failures, output-bundle layout, and Quarto rendering. It does not prove independent report reproduction.
- `tests/fixtures/synthetic_report_baseline/` is a richer fixture. It proves artifact grouping into the `do_report(...)` wrapper path without real locations or beneficiary-sensitive values.
- `known-good-baselines/<case>/` is the ignored local baseline root for real exports. It should not be committed.

Current local coverage examples:

- `known-good-baselines/melissa-jam/`: operational Melissa/Jamaica case; passes provisionally.
- `known-good-baselines/melissa-jam-2025102718/`: same storm and country, different forecast time; passes provisionally.
- `known-good-baselines/melissa-cub-2025102800/`: different country with full facility layers; passes provisionally.
- `known-good-baselines/melissa-tca-2025102800/`: small-island/edge-geography case with zero shelter rows; passes provisionally.

An independent Melissa/Jamaica report from Snowflake stage now produces `certifying_comparison` when the baseline includes the independent current report, a previous report via `previous_report_path`, and vulnerability MAT artifacts. Equal-probability top facility descriptor order may still appear as warnings.

## Snapshot Workflow

Run a smoke snapshot:

```bash
uv run aots-report snapshot \
  --baseline tests/fixtures/synthetic_baseline \
  --out /tmp/aots-report-smoke
```

Run a snapshot against a real local baseline:

```bash
uv run aots-report snapshot \
  --baseline known-good-baselines/melissa-jam \
  --out /tmp/aots-report-melissa-jam
```

Read `/tmp/aots-report-melissa-jam/comparison.json` before trusting the output. A passing comparison is certifying only when `certifying` is `true` and `certification_state` is `certifying_comparison`.

## Snowflake Export Workflow

Preview a Snowflake export plan without connecting:

```bash
uv run aots-report export-snowflake \
  --country JAM \
  --storm MELISSA \
  --forecast-time '2025-10-28 00:00:00' \
  --case-name melissa-jam \
  --env-file .env \
  --dry-run \
  --json
```

Run the export:

```bash
uv run aots-report export-snowflake \
  --country JAM \
  --storm MELISSA \
  --forecast-time '2025-10-28 00:00:00' \
  --case-name melissa-jam \
  --env-file .env \
  --overwrite
```

Include the Snowflake alert-agent email HTML when a matching alert exists in `ALERT_SENT_LOG`:

```bash
uv run aots-report export-snowflake \
  --country JAM \
  --storm MELISSA \
  --forecast-time '2025-10-28 00:00:00' \
  --case-name melissa-jam \
  --env-file .env \
  --include-alert-html \
  --overwrite
```

This writes `expected-alert.html` and records `expected_alert_path` in `manifest.json`. The snapshot command copies that independent Snowflake alert-agent email artifact into the Snapshot Output Bundle so Playwright or another browser tool can visually inspect it directly.

When `expected-alert.html` is present, `snapshot` also writes a separate local alert artifact plus an alert audit bundle:

- `rendered-alert.html`: locally generated alert HTML using baseline-replayed prose for the first slice.
- `alert-context.json`: structured inputs used to render the local alert.
- `alert-claims.json`: normalized factual claims used for alert parity.
- `alert-comparison.json`: claim and DOM-presence comparison results.
- `alert-assets/*.png`: generated alert visuals for audit/debug when the baseline has enough source data. The same PNG bytes are embedded inline in `rendered-alert.html` as base64 data URIs for email portability.

The generated snapshot `manifest.json` records relative paths for these alert files only when they are emitted, so alert-missing bundles stay portable without dangling alert entries.

Alert parity is intentionally not byte-for-byte HTML or pixel parity. It blocks on significant factual differences or omissions and treats exact prose wording or visual layout differences as review concerns.

Visual parity follows the same rule: `alert-comparison.json` fails when a required visual section is missing despite available source data. Unavailable optional visual inputs should produce warnings rather than block the snapshot.

See [Comparison Cases](comparison-cases.qmd) for real JAM/CUB/PHL comparison results and committed Playwright screenshots for the two cases that had Snowflake alert-agent emails.

Do not pass passwords as CLI arguments. Use `SNOWFLAKE_*` variables from the shell or `--env-file <path>`.

## Publication Workflow

First generate one or more Snapshot Output Bundles:

```bash
uv run aots-report snapshot \
  --baseline known-good-baselines/melissa-jam \
  --out /tmp/aots-snapshots/melissa-jam
```

Then publish an index over those bundles:

```bash
uv run aots-report publish \
  --snapshots-dir /tmp/aots-snapshots \
  --out /tmp/aots-publication
```

`publish` does not consume raw baseline directories. Baselines are source inputs; Snapshot Output Bundles are publication inputs.

## Common Failure Modes

- `missing Snowflake configuration`: fill in `SNOWFLAKE_*` values in `.env` or your shell environment.
- `refusing to overwrite`: pass `--overwrite` only after confirming the target baseline directory can be replaced.
- `missing required artifacts`: the baseline is not complete enough for validation.
- `checksum mismatch`: a source artifact changed after the manifest was written.
- `schema mismatch` or `row count mismatch`: the manifest no longer describes the artifact on disk.
- `comparison.status == failed`: inspect `comparison.json` and `comparison.md`; do not publish as a trusted report.

## Safety Notes

- Real baselines may include facility-level or operationally sensitive data. Keep them in ignored local directories unless a sharing policy says otherwise.
- Current Quarto output is an audit/debug rendering, not a finished public report.
- Before external or broad internal publication, apply the privacy, accessibility, and public-interest gates in [Snowflake-Agnostic Report Publication](snowflake-agnostic-report-publication.qmd).

## Agent Setup

Agent instructions live in `AGENTS.md`. Model/provider defaults live in `.agents/models.yml`.

Configured harnesses:

- `opencode`
- `paseo`

OpenCode project config lives in `opencode.json`. It registers `.agents/skills` and includes MCP entries for Playwright, CQ, Headroom, and Context7. Context7 expects `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` to be provided by the user environment, not committed to the repository.

Paseo is a machine-level orchestration harness. This repository records Paseo compatibility, but provider preferences, schedules, daemon settings, and managed worktree roots stay in user-owned `~/.paseo` config outside the repository.

## Installed Skills

Vendored skills live under `.agents/skills/`:

- `a11y-web-scan` for accessibility scan planning and review of web outputs.
- `caveman` for ultra-compressed communication mode.
- `cq` for querying and recording shared agent knowledge.
- `diagnose` for disciplined debugging and performance regression loops.
- `get-api-docs` for current third-party API, SDK, and library documentation lookup.
- `grill-with-docs` for stress-testing plans against project language and docs.
- `improve-codebase-architecture` for architecture deepening reviews.
- `liteparse` for local parsing/conversion of unstructured files.
- `prompt-eval-design`, `prompt-migration`, and `prompt-output-safety` for prompt-heavy work.
- `security-audit` for security, secret, dependency, auth, and authorization review.
- `session-focus` for keeping multi-step agent work scoped.
- `tdd` for red-green-refactor workflows.
- `to-issues` and `to-prd` for issue/PRD creation from plans and context.
- `zoom-out` for higher-level codebase/context orientation.

## Tool Profiles

Tool setup guidance lives in `.agents/tools.yml` and covers CQ, accessibility scanning, browser automation, Headroom context compression/MCP/proxy workflows, OpenCode MCP entries, OpenCode Homebrew PATH guidance, and Playwright MCP usage.
